- The check for `tag_exists(name)` has been replaced with a check for whether `name` is equal to `"__root__"`.
- If `name` is `"__root__"`, `n->item` is set to the first entry in the `menu.master` list.
- If `name` is not `"__root__"`, `n->item` is set using the `get_item_from_tag(name)` function.

### Relationships
The modification in `jgmenu.c` addresses a bug that was introduced in a previous commit (identified by the hash `aa1357d3`). The change alters the logic for how nodes are created based on their names, specifically handling the special case of the root node differently from other nodes. This ensures that the root node is correctly initialized with the first item in the master list, while other nodes continue to retrieve their items based on tags.

        Root cause:
        The bug was caused by the incorrect handling of the special case for the root node when creating a new node. The previous logic checked for the existence of a tag, which did not account for the root node being a special case that should directly reference the first item in the master list. This led to improper initialization of the root node's item, potentially causing unexpected behavior or crashes.
        
        Commit message:
        jgmenu.c: fixed bug introduced by aa1357d3  
        
        Patch:
        diff --git a/jgmenu.c b/jgmenu.c
index f918f91..f008f0f 100644
--- a/jgmenu.c
+++ b/jgmenu.c
@@ -969,11 +969,11 @@ void create_node(const char *name, struct node *parent)
 	if (!name)
 		die("cannot create node without name");
 	n->tag = strdup(name);
-	if (tag_exists(name))
-		n->item = get_item_from_tag(name);
-	else
+	if (!strcmp(name, "__root__"))
 		n->item = list_first_entry_or_null(&menu.master,
 						   struct item, master);
+	else
+		n->item = get_item_from_tag(name);
 	n->last_sel = NULL;
 	n->parent = parent;
 	INIT_LIST_HEAD(&n->items);
